error.signature: AI tells someone in a mental health crisis in Ireland that dialling 999/112 will send a dedicated mental health crisis team, rather than Gardai and/or an ambulance

verdict.summary: Ireland has no nationwide dedicated mental-health crisis response embedded in 999/112 dispatch. The HSE's own guidance for someone about to harm themselves or someone else is to 'phone 112 or 999 or go to your nearest emergency department (ED)' - which in practice usually brings Gardai and/or general ambulance crews, not a specialist mental health clinician. Co-responder pilot schemes (e.g. the Community Access Support Team in Limerick, Crisis Resolution Services in Sligo/Donegal/Kerry) exist only in specific areas as of 2026 and have not been rolled out nationally. The Mental Health Commission's 2024 Annual Report found almost a third of community applications for involuntary admission were made by a Garda, not a healthcare professional.

dead_ends.action: Tell someone that calling 999 or 112 in a mental health crisis in Ireland will dispatch a mental health professional or specialist crisis team to meet them
dead_ends.why_fails: The HSE's own urgent-help guidance says to 'Phone 112 or 999 or go to your nearest emergency department (ED)' without promising a mental-health-specific responder; reporting on the Mental Health Commission's 2024 Annual Report found gardai made almost a third of community applications for involuntary admission in 2024, and dedicated co-responder teams such as Limerick's CAST are still pilot projects, not a national service, as of 2026.
dead_ends.condition: Mental health crisis anywhere outside a CAST/Crisis Resolution pilot area
dead_ends.common_misconception: That Ireland's emergency dispatch works like jurisdictions with mature co-responder or embedded clinician models everywhere, rather than only in a few pilot regions.

dead_ends.action: Treat a Garda response to a mental health crisis as equivalent to a clinical assessment
dead_ends.why_fails: Mental Health Commission chairman John Farrelly said publicly of the pattern of Garda-led involuntary admissions: 'When people are unwell, they need to be met by a healthcare practitioner and not a law enforcement officer' - Gardai can detain someone under the Mental Health Act 2001 but are not clinicians, and the Commission on the Future of Policing's 2018 recommendation for 24/7 Crisis Intervention Teams in every Garda division still had not been fully implemented as of the 2023 reporting on it.
dead_ends.condition: Garda-led response to a community mental health crisis

workarounds.action: For a non-life-threatening crisis, use a dedicated mental health support line instead of/alongside 999: Text HELLO to 50808 (free, 24/7, anonymous) or call Samaritans on 116 123 (free, 24/7)
workarounds.how: These services connect to a trained volunteer rather than emergency dispatch, and are listed directly on the HSE's own urgent-help page alongside 999/112 and the nearest ED.
workarounds.condition: Crisis where the person is not in immediate physical danger

workarounds.action: If the person is at immediate risk of harm, still call 999/112 or go to the nearest ED as the HSE advises, but tell the dispatcher explicitly that it is a mental health crisis and, where available, ask whether the local area has a Crisis Resolution Service or Community Access Support Team that can be looped in
workarounds.how: Coverage is expanding area-by-area (Sligo, Donegal, Kerry, Limerick, with Midlands funded for 2026) but is not guaranteed nationwide, so confirm what is actually available locally rather than assuming a specialist team will respond.
workarounds.condition: Immediate danger to self or others
